text:
maria-support: FYI — BlueCart reporting 403s on their webhook endpoints since our NAT maintenance window last night. They say source IPs changed and their firewall is blocking. Can network take a look? :rotating_light:

bluecart-sre: We started seeing failures ~02:20Z. Our security team only allows three IPs; requests are now coming from 34.201.45.67 and 44.55.66.77 which are not on the allowlist. Example curl response below.
```
> curl -v https://hooks.bluecart.example.com/push -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
* Connected to hooks.bluecart.example.com (34.201.45.67) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
> GET /push HTTP/1.1
> Host: hooks.bluecart.example.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.82.0
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< x-redwood-source-ip: 34.201.45.67
{ "error": "ip_not_allowed" }
```

alex-net: Thanks. Checking our egress rotation logs now. Can you confirm the exact timestamps you saw failures?

bluecart-sre: Failures started 2026-03-15T02:18Z and persisted until ~02:40Z when we temporarily relaxed the firewall to test.

deploy-bot: NAT-rotation-job completed for vpc-prod-1 at 2026-03-15T02:13:02Z. Old pool: [3.4.5.6, 3.4.5.7, 3.4.5.8], New pool: [34.201.45.67, 44.55.66.77, 52.12.99.101].

jon-oncall: Looks like the rotation swapped the egress pool. Should have been transparent but customer has a strict allowlist. Did the runbook include customer notification?

maria-support: We sent a maintenance notice for the window but didn't call out IP churn — we assumed ephemeral IPs. Customer SLA requires static egress. They escalated immediately.

alex-net: Reproduced locally by running a curl from a test instance in the same subnet using current SNAT. Confirmed source IP matches deploy-bot's new pool. Repro steps: run from rear subnet in vpc-prod-1: `curl -sS -D - https://ifconfig.io/ip` returns one of new pool IPs.

lisa-engineering: Quick mitigation options: 1) Ask BlueCart to add the new pool IPs to their allowlist (fast, manual). 2) Provision customer a dedicated static egress (Dedicated-egress / reserved NAT) — longer lead. 3) Proxy webhooks through hosted endpoint that won't rotate egress.

kevin-psr: I'm on the account — I'll coordinate the PSR. Action items: open a support ticket with the new IPs, offer a 48h temporary IP allowlist window, escalate provisioning for dedicated egress if they want a permanent fix. I'll draft the email.

maria-support: Can we provide a signed statement of the IPs and rotation timeline for their security team? They asked for audit proof.

alex-net: Yes — I'll attach the rotation job logs and the deployment audit. Also include CIDR and exact timestamps.

bluecart-sre: We updated our firewall with the three IPs you listed and tested — callbacks started succeeding at 02:45Z, looks good now. We'll still request a non-rotating option for production.

jon-oncall: Root cause: intended NAT egress rotation applied to prod pool during maintenance window; we didn't flag customer with static egress requirement. Follow-ups: (1) Add a field to the maintenance playbook to surface customers with allowlists tied to prod VPCs. (2) Add a checkbox to outbound rotation runbook to exempt reserved egress customers.

lisa-engineering: I'll file a quick RFC to add an opt-out for egress rotation and a console flag to request static egress for webhooks.

kevin-psr: Customer emailed back: "We're fine with the temporary update, please proceed with dedicated egress provisioning." I've created PSR-2345 and linked the account. ETA on provisioning?

alex-net: We can schedule dedicated egress within 5 business days if capacity is available; I'll check with infra schedule and confirm by EOD.

maria-support: Closing loop here — BlueCart confirmed callbacks resumed after they allowed the IPs. Keeping thread open until dedicated egress confirmed. :white_check_mark:
